([[Jersey City, New Jersey]]) | college = [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] (2022–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team1 = [[Long Island Nets]] | highlights = * [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman team (2023) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|2022 Mexico]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} | team2 = [[Texas Legends]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present }} '''Mark Armstrong''' (born February 21, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]]. ==Early life and high school career== Armstrong grew up in [[South Orange, New Jersey]] and attended [[St. Peter's Preparatory School]] in [[Jersey City, New Jersey]].{{cite web|first=Maria|last=McIlwain|title=Villanova recruits Mark Armstrong and Cam Whitmore stuck to their commitments|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/villanova-basketball-recruiting-mark-armstrong-cam-whitmore-20220602.html|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=June 2, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} He was a four-year starter on the basketball team and averaged 15.9 points per game as a freshman. Armstrong was named third-team All-State after averaging 19.9 points per game during his sophomore season.{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Bernstein|title=St. Peter’s Prep junior Mark Armstrong scores his 1,000th point|url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2021/01/st-peters-prep-junior-mark-armstrong-scores-his-1000th-point.html|work=[[The Jersey Journal]]|date=January 30, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2023}} He averaged 14.1 points, 2.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 2.2 steals in eleven games during his junior season, which was shortened due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Bernstein|title=Mark Armstrong soars to the St. Peter’s Prep career scoring record|url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2022/02/mark-armstrong-soars-to-the-st-peters-prep-career-scoring-record.html|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=February 26, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} Armstrong was named the [[Hudson County Interscholastic League]] Player the Year as a senior after averaging 23.4 points, five rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game.{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Godin|title=Villanova Basketball 2022-23 Player Preview: Mark Armstrong|url=https://www.vuhoops.com/villanova-basketball/2022/10/12/23399636/villanova-basketball-2022-23-player-preview-mark-armstrong|website=VUHoops.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 12, 2022|access-date=January 16, 2023}} ===Recruiting=== Armstrong was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and a consensus top-75 prospect by major recruiting services.{{cite web|first=C.J.|last=Holmes|title=What Villanova is getting in 4-star point guard Mark Armstrong, a 2022 commitment|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2522021/2021/04/19/what-villanova-is-getting-in-4-star-point-guard-mark-armstrong-a-2022-commitment/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=April 19, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2023}} On April 8, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] over offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Juliano|title=New Jersey combination guard Mark Armstrong commits to Villanova for 2022|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/mark-armstrong-commitment-villanova-basketball-20210408.html|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=April 8, | accessdate = December 11, 2023 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Armstrong began his freshman season at Villanova as a key reserve.{{cite web|title=South Orange's Mark Armstrong Impresses as a Villanova Wildcat|url=https://villagegreennj.com/towns/south-orange/south-oranges-mark-armstrong-impresses-as-a-villanova-wildcat/|website=[[The Village Green (news site)|The Village Green]]|date=December 11, 2022|access-date=January 13, 2023}} He started six of the team's seven games in December before returning to a backup role.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=O'Neil|title=Cam Whitmore is back, Mark Armstrong is starting and Villanova gets a necessary win|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3965839/2022/12/03/cam-whitmore-mark-armstrong-villanova/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=December 3, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2022}} He was named the [[Big East Conference]] Freshman of the Week after scoring 10 points on 3-of-4 shooting from the field in his first career start against [[2022–23 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]].{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Godin|title=Catching up with the ‘Cats: From Team USA to Main Line, Whitmore, Armstrong look to leave their mark, and other Villanova updates|url=https://www.vuhoops.com/villanova-basketball/2022/12/6/23497318/catching-up-with-the-cats-whitmore-armstrong-dixon-villanova-wildcats-college-basketball|website=VUHoops.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=December 6, 2022|access-date=January 13, 2023}} Armstrong was named to the Big East All-Freshman team at the end of the regular season.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Neiburg|title=Villanova forward Cam Whitmore named top Big East freshman|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/villanova-cam-whitmore-highlights-freshman-of-the-year-big-east-tournament-20230308.html|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 8, 2023|access-date=March 15, 2023}} ==Professional career== === Long Island Nets (2024–2025) === After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Armstrong joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Announce 2024 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-2024-summer-league-roster|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=October 9, 2024}} and on October 9, 2024, he signed with the team.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Nets Sign, Waive Mark Armstrong|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/nets-sign-mark-armstrong.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 14, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2024}} However, he was waived four days later and on October 27, he joined the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite tweet|author=Long Island Nets|title=Our official training camp roster 🔥 #StrongIsland 💪|number=1850674269581197342|user=LongIslandNets|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} === Texas Legends (2025–present) === On September 19, 2025, Armstrong was traded to the [[Texas Legends]] in exchange for the returning player rights to [[Max Fiedler (basketball)|Max Fiedler]] and a 2026 second-round pick.{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2025 |title=Texas Legends Trade For Mark Armstrong |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DOzMFN6kSEq/?igsh=c25zbWNkdzQxdG9o}} ==National team career== Armstrong played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]].{{cite web|first=Josh|last=Naso|title=Cam Whitmore, Mark Armstrong make USA Basketball U18 team|url=https://villanova.rivals.com/news/cam-whitmore-mark-armstrong-make-usa-basketball-u18-team|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=May 31, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2022}} He averaged 10.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game as the United States won the gold medal.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=N.J. prep star, Villanova commit Mark Armstrong wins gold medal with USA U18 National Team|url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2022/06/nj-prep-star-villanova-commit-mark-armstrong-wins-gold-medal-with-usa-u18-national-team.html|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=June 13, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2022}} Armstrong was also named to the United States' roster for the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Greene|title=Dylan Harper, Mark Armstrong Make USA National Basketball Team|url=https://www.tapinto.net/towns/nutley/sections/sports/articles/dylan-harper-mark-armstrong-make-usa-national-basketball-team|website=TAPinto.net|date=June 17, 2023|access-date=June 21, 2023}}
